title: Kerala Land Reforms S.81 Exemption Protection for Rubber Holdings
legalPropositions: Rubber plantation land is statutorily exempted under Section 81.

citations.proposition: Plantation character is determined on vesting date.

author: Adv. Meera Krishnan
summary: Plantation exemption under Section 81(1)(e) remains immune from ceiling surrender.

title: Telegraph Act Section 16 Injunction & Mandatory Magistrate Referral
author: Adv. Meera Krishnan
summary: Precedent synthesis establishing that the transmission licensee has no authority to proceed with high-tension line drawing over agricultural holdings upon resistance without obtaining a prior order from the District Magistrate under Section 16(1).
legalPropositions: Transmission licensee acquires only right of user under Section 10(b), not proprietary ownership.
Upon objection by landowner or lawful occupier, work must be paused and referred to District Magistrate.
Land diminution compensation under Section 10(d) & 16(3) is mandatory for line corridor restriction.

citations.proposition: Telegraph authority has no power to adjudicate landowner resistance unilaterally.
Permanent diminution in land market value must be assessed under Section 10(d).

citations.citation: Power Grid Corp of India v. Century Textiles Ltd
citations.proposition: Section 164 Electricity Act confers Telegraph Act powers subject to Section 10/16 safeguards.

title: Invalidity of Unilateral Arbitrator Appointment Clause in Commercial Contracts
author: Adv. Meera Krishnan
summary: Authority bundle establishing that unilateral appointment of a sole arbitrator by one party or its Managing Director is void ab initio under Section 12(5) read with Seventh Schedule of the 1996 Act.
legalPropositions: A party interested in dispute outcome cannot unilaterally nominate a sole arbitrator.
Ineligible nominee cannot be cured by private contract terms without post-dispute written waiver.
The competent High Court under Section 11(6) must appoint an independent sole arbitrator.

citations.citation: Perkins Eastman Architects DPC v. HSCC (India) Ltd.
citations.proposition: A person disqualified from acting as arbitrator cannot nominate an arbitrator.

citations.citation: TRF Limited v. Energo Engineering Projects Ltd.
citations.proposition: Statutory disqualification under Section 12(5) renders nomination authority void.

citations.citation: Bharat Broadband Network Ltd. v. United Telecoms Ltd.
citations.proposition: Express agreement in writing required for waiver under Section 12(5) proviso.

title: Section 482 BNSS Anticipatory Bail for Commercial Dishonour / Cheating Allegations
author: Adv. Meera Krishnan
summary: Synthesis of High Court and Supreme Court authorities guarding against criminalization of civil contractual breaches under IPC 420 / BNS 318 where Section 138 NI Act remedy exists.
legalPropositions: Mere failure to repay a loan or dishonour of a cheque does not constitute cheating without fraudulent intent from inception.
Simultaneous invocation of Section 138 NI Act and criminal cheating requires strict scrutiny to prevent abuse of process.
Custodial interrogation is unwarranted where transaction is fully evidenced by bank statements and contracts.

citations.proposition: Breach of contractual promise does not amount to cheating without dishonest inception.

citations.citation: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
citations.proposition: Arrest cannot be made mechanically for offences punishable with up to 7 years imprisonment.

citations.citation: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi)
citations.proposition: Anticipatory bail should not ordinarily be restricted to a predetermined time period.

title: Specific Performance & Discretionary Injunction under Specific Relief Act 1963
author: Adv. Rajesh V. Varma
summary: Analysis of Section 10 post-2018 amendment to Specific Relief Act removing judicial discretion in enforcing valid immovable property agreements.
legalPropositions: Specific performance of contracts is mandatory post-2018 amendment unless barred by Section 11, 14, or 16.
Injunction against alienation pendente lite is necessary to preserve property status quo under Section 52 TP Act.

citations.proposition: Post-2018 amendment, court is bound to enforce specific performance of contracts.

citations.citation: Maharwal Khewaji Trust v. Baldev Dass
citations.proposition: Status quo must be maintained unless irreparable loss is demonstrated.
